summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Kriti Dangi
  • Channel: Agentic AI Foundation
  • Main topic: Building an AI-powered debugging agent harness (DebugAssist) at Uber using 11 MCP servers
  • Purpose: To share Uber's architecture, challenges, and impact of deploying autonomous agents for app quality and production bug resolution at scale. Uber senior software engineer Kriti Dangi presents DebugAssist, an AI-powered debugging agent harness built at Uber to tackle production crash investigations and reduce mean time to resolve issues. The system automates end-to-end debugging across discovery, auto-triage, deep root cause analysis (RCA) using models like Claude, and resolution, utilizing LangGraph combined with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and deterministic-AI hybrid pipelines.

Topic Map

Debugging in Reality at Uber

  • Explanation: Discusses the severe challenges of software debugging in massive mono-repo codebases with scattered context, unclear error messages, and cross-team dependencies.
  • Key claims:
    • Uber engineers take an average of 28 days to resolve an issue.
    • Developers spend 40% of their time debugging and fixing production issues.
    • Monorepo architecture means many teams contribute to a single repository, making ownership difficult to trace.
  • Examples:
    • Receiving PagerDuty alerts at 2 AM with vague stack traces or blank screens.
  • Terminology:
    • Wisdom
    • Healthline
    • monorepo
    • RCA
  • Why it matters: Explains why automated agentic debugging is critical for developer productivity and app stability.

DebugAssist End-to-End Agentic Resolution Journey

  • Explanation: Walks through the four stages of bug resolution: Discovery, Auto-Triage, DebugAssist (Deep RCA), and Resolution.
  • Key claims:
    • Discovery captures crashes and user feedback via internal tools Healthline and Wisdom.
    • Auto-triage identifies severity, customer impact, and routes to the correct JIRA team.
    • DebugAssist performs deep RCA in under 30 minutes by analyzing stack traces, logs, and metadata.
  • Examples:
    • A developer reporting extreme battery usage via Slack gets an auto-generated fix on the same day.
  • Terminology:
    • Discovery
    • Auto-triage
    • Root Cause Analysis
    • JIRA
  • Why it matters: Establishes a standardized, automated workflow from bug report to deployed fix.

Under the Hood: Agent Pipeline & MCP Servers

  • Explanation: Details the LangGraph-based hybrid pipeline combining deterministic nodes and LLM nodes with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
  • Key claims:
    • Pipelines use LangGraph to bypass the planning phase and enforce deterministic steps, reducing LLM hallucination.
    • Deterministic context collection queries Jaeger, distributed tracing, and logging via MCP connections.
    • Sub-agents fan out in parallel to analyze breadcrumbs, crash correlation, and git history.
  • Examples:
    • ClassifyRCA runs on Claude Sonnet with limited turns; fixing runs on Claude Opus with higher max turns.
  • Terminology:
    • LangGraph
    • MCP servers
    • Claude Sonnet
    • Claude Opus
    • PEX binaries
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates how to productionize AI agents reliably at Uber scale without uncontrolled agent loops.

Productionization at Uber Scale & UX Features

  • Explanation: Explains how 8 agent types are packaged into Python PEX binaries, pushed to Artifactory, and run across monorepos with built-in human-in-the-loop UX features.
  • Key claims:
    • All code resides in Python monorepos and is packaged as PEX binaries executed via Docker runtimes.
    • UX features include Diff fixer for incremental adjustments, Ask AI Chat for developer feedback loops, and Open in your Machine.
    • MCP plugin loading is restricted at runtime to prevent context bloat.
  • Examples:
    • Refactoring code or adding unit tests with a single click in the Diff fixer.
  • Terminology:
    • PEX
    • Artifactory
    • Diff fixer
    • Ask AI Chat
    • domain extensions
  • Why it matters: Shows how complex AI systems are reliably deployed, versioned, and interacted with by developers.

Impact & Metrics

  • Explanation: Shares metrics on the impact of DebugAssist on Uber's engineering velocity and issue resolution quality.
  • Key claims:
    • DebugAssist handles ~9,000 RCAs per month.
    • RCA accuracy is 50% compared against exact developer fixes, with 40% in the right direction.
    • JIRA resolution time improved by 2x.
    • PR merge rate for agent-fixed issues increased from 5% to 48%.
  • Examples:
    • Clearing backlogs of out-of-SLA issues and increasing PR merges.
  • Terminology:
    • RCA accuracy
    • PR merge rate
    • mean time to resolve
  • Why it matters: Proves the tangible business and engineering value of AI-powered debugging.

Key Points

Deterministic-AI Hybrid Pipelines

  • Explanation: Combining LangGraph deterministic skeletons with LLM nodes avoids hallucination and keeps token costs and latency under control.
  • Evidence: Pipeline enforces exact steps (Context Collector -> ClassifyRCA -> Fix -> Bazel Test -> Create Diff).
  • Practical implication: Engineers can build reliable agents that do not wander into infinite rabbit holes.

Scale and Productionization

  • Explanation: Agents are packaged as Python PEX binaries stored in Artifactory and executed using Docker image registries.
  • Evidence: 8 agent types running across 5 monorepos handling 9,000 RCAs per month.
  • Practical implication: Allows seamless deployment and execution of AI workloads across massive enterprise infrastructure.

Human-in-the-Loop UX

  • Explanation: Providing tools like Diff fixer, Ask AI chat, and one-click machine deployment ensures developers stay in control while saving hours of manual work.
  • Evidence: PR merge rate increased from 5% to 48% as developers gained interactive feedback loops.
  • Practical implication: Developers are much more likely to adopt and trust AI-generated fixes when they can easily review and tweak them.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

DebugAssist Agent Pipeline

  • How it works: A LangGraph workflow that executes deterministic context collection, AI classification, fixing, validation testing, and diff creation.
  • Components:
    • Context Collector
    • ClassifyRCA
    • Fix
    • Bazel Test (Validation)
    • Create Diff
  • When to use: For automated triage, root cause analysis, and patch generation of software production crashes.

Examples & Case Studies

An Uber developer experienced excessive battery usage due to the Android app running background loops during a ride.

  • Illustrates: End-to-end agentic discovery, auto-triage, deep RCA, and same-day PR creation.
  • Lesson: AI agents can isolate hot-looping code paths and generate fixes before the developer even opens their laptop at the office.

A P1 crash caused by disk full cache write errors during push notifications was caught at 5% rollout.

  • Illustrates: High-severity crash detection and rapid fix deployment.
  • Lesson: Automated debugging prevents widespread customer-impacting outages by catching bad rollouts early.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Use deterministic skeletons in agent workflows to restrict LLM wandering.
    • Preprocess large log files before passing them to agents to reduce token costs and noise.
  • Strategic:
    • Provide harness infrastructure while allowing teams to plug in their own domain-specific agent skills.
    • Focus on human-in-the-loop developer UX (diff fixers, chat, local execution) to drive high PR merge rates.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How to scale domain extensions for thousands of distinct microservice owners?
    • How to further improve RCA accuracy from 50% to near 100%?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Engineers spend 40% of their time debugging according to Stripe report (statistic)
  • DebugAssist handles 9,000 RCAs per month with 48% PR merge rate (internal metric)

Notable Quotes

"MCP-Powered Crash Investigation: How 11 MCP Servers Help an AI Agent Debug Production Issues at Uber" "DebugAssist is a AI agent for debugging that we built at Uber." "An engineer at Uber takes almost 28 days to resolve an issue on an average."

Compressed Summary

  • DebugAssist is Uber's AI agent harness for debugging production crashes.
  • Combines LangGraph deterministic pipelines with LLM nodes to prevent hallucinations.
  • Utilizes 11 MCP servers for accessing logs, traces, and internal tools.
  • Handles 9,000 RCAs per month with a 48% PR merge rate and 2x faster JIRA resolution.
  • Keywords: debugging, ai agent, langgraph, mcp, uber
  • Core insight: Combining deterministic graph pipelines with specialized AI agents and MCP servers transforms reactive production debugging into automated, same-day resolution at enterprise scale.
